subject: tunnel boring machine
title: A 6,700-Ton Tunnel Drill Got Stuck Under Seattle for Two Years

scenes.text: A 6,700-ton drill stopped dead under Seattle. For two years.
Bertha's cutting face was 57 feet across, boring a 1.7-mile highway tunnel under downtown.
In December 2013, about a thousand feet in, it overheated and stopped.
It had struck a forgotten steel pipe, and grit had wrecked the seals around its main bearing.
So engineers dug a 120-foot pit in front of it and lifted its 2,000-ton front end out.
Repaired, Bertha started digging again in December 2015, and finished the tunnel in 2017.

description:
Bertha, a 57.5-foot-wide tunnel boring machine weighing 6,700 tons, stalled under Seattle in December 2013 after about 1,000 feet.
Engineers dug a 120-foot rescue shaft and hoisted its front end, a lift of about 2,200 tons, to the surface in March 2015. It resumed in December 2015 and broke through in April 2017.
Would you have tried to fix it or start over?
first_comment: The steel pipe it hit was an 8-inch well casing left behind by a groundwater study in 2002. After the tunnel was done, most of Bertha was melted down for scrap. Should they have kept it as a monument?
